findings.title: AI Agents Are Hacking Online Retailers for $25 a Company
findings.summary_md: Gambit Security's threat intelligence team reconstructed an ongoing campaign in which a financially motivated operator used the Hermes, Strix, and Cairn AI harnesses to attack hundreds of online retailers at a marginal cost of about $25 per company. Between September 10 and 15, 2026, 105 attack projects were launched and at least 27 companies were compromised to varying degrees, with more than 600,000 credit card records stolen from two victims and card skimmers injected on at least 19 sites. The activity dates back to July 2026 and involved DeepSeek and GLM models accessed through OpenRouter, with total model spend estimated between $12,000 and $18,000. Gambit also documented a wipe-after-extraction routine that deleted Magento payment data and dropped 180 tables at one retailer, including backups.

findings.title: Inside Cairn: Open Windows into massive AI-Driven Cyber Operations
findings.summary_md: NorForge's investigation into publicly exposed Cairn control panels identified more than 20 panels likely used in malicious operations, including a Chinese-language cluster (AIA0001) of 14 panels tied to over 1,100 attack projects against e-commerce sites in the US, Japan, and Australia. The AIA0001 cluster used a worker named claudecode_deepseek-v4.1-flash and achieved an average success rate near 10 percent, with successful intrusions averaging under 23 hours and about 140 facts per project. Trufflehog over the exposed panel data found hundreds of secrets, 11 percent verified as still valid, and the panels appeared to expose full administrative controls for starting, stopping, and redirecting agents. NorForge verified a live uploader web shell on a large hardware-parts vendor's site and independently confirmed the compromise of a very large US retailer.

findings.title: EXCLUSIVE: How one hacker used AI agents and a few thousand dollars to break into scores of sites
findings.summary_md: Reuters reported that a Chinese-speaking hacker used autonomous AI agents to attempt to breach more than 1,200 websites and gained access to sites belonging to more than 100 companies, including Deere, SharkNinja, and Cummins. The operator's own records showed roughly $5,000 in token spending, or about $50 per successful compromise, and instructions were sketched in fewer than 100 Chinese characters. Cairn, the open-source tool used, lets agents work toward a goal step by step and post findings to a shared board, and its author said it was not designed for hacking. Reuters reviewed the attacker's artifacts and named victims from its own review of the activity.
